# Evolution by natural selection (`evolution_natural_selection`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/biology.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Life sciences (`biology`)
- Deps: helped by deep_time_geology, selective_breeding, taxonomy, heredity_genetics, world_geography
- Core idea: All living kinds descend, with gradual change, from earlier kinds, and are related like branches of one tree. The mechanism needs no purpose: individuals of a kind differ; some differences are inherited; far more are born than can survive; those whose inherited traits suit the conditions leave more offspring, so over many generations the population shifts. Breeders do the same on purpose and have made the greyhound and the lapdog from one stock in a few thousand years; nature has had hundreds of millions. Evidence: fossils in rock layers change in order; a human arm, a bat's wing and a whale's flipper have the same bones; useless remnants persist; islands hold their own species resembling those of the nearest mainland.
- Pitfalls:
  - Saying humans descend from today's monkeys; they share ancestors
  - Describing animals as striving or needing to change (the giraffe stretching its neck); selection acts on variation that is already there
  - Presenting evolution as a ladder of progress with man at the top
  - Reading 'survival of the fittest' as 'might is right' and applying it to nations or classes
  - Forgetting that Darwin could not explain inheritance or variation, the weak point his critics attacked
- History: greece: 5th c. BC – Empedocles imagines unfit forms dying out; speculation without mechanism of descent; islamic: 9th c. – al-Jahiz describes the struggle for existence among animals; modern claims that he or Ibn Khaldun had a theory of evolution are overstated; europe: 1809 – Lamarck's transformation by use and disuse; 1831 Matthew states selection in an appendix on timber; 1858 Darwin and Wallace's joint papers; 1859 On the Origin of Species; 1930s–1940s synthesis with genetics; east_asia: 1858 – Wallace writes his selection essay at Ternate in the Moluccas
- Read:
  - Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1859)
  - Peter J. Bowler, Evolution: The History of an Idea (1984)
  - Jonathan Weiner, The Beak of the Finch (1994)
